literal: If [I] despise [him], it will be a disgrace, thinking thus, my life-loving heart thinks of his virtues.
translation: Thinking that it would be a disgrace to despise him, my life-loving heart thinks only of his virtues.
modern: அவரை இகழ்ந்து பேசினால் அது நமக்கு இழிவாகும் என்று நினைத்து, என் உயிர் மேல் ஆசை கொண்ட நெஞ்சம் அவருடைய நற்குணங்களையே நினைத்துப் பார்க்கிறது.
explanation: In this couplet, the heroine speaks of her heart's inability to stay angry with her beloved. She notes that if she were to despise or blame him for his absence, it would only bring disgrace to their love. To avoid this humiliation and to preserve its own life, her heart, which is deeply attached to living, chooses to focus entirely on his good qualities. The phrase 'uyirkkātal neñcu' highlights how the heart clings to life by choosing love and positive remembrance over resentment.
